tagline: Australia's largest city wraps a glittering harbour around the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, with famous beaches minutes from downtown. It is ranked #21 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Sydney began in 1788 as a British penal colony at Sydney Cove. The Rocks district preserves the old convict-era streets, while the skyline is now defined by the Opera House's white sails and the steel arch of the Harbour Bridge, opened in 1932.

The harbour is the city's heart. Ferries cross to Manly and Watsons Bay past waterfront mansions and hidden coves. For the full view, climb the Harbour Bridge's arch — one of the world's most famous bridge climbs — or take in the skyline from the Royal Botanic Garden at Mrs Macquarie's Chair.

Life here revolves around the coast. Bondi Beach is a bus ride from the centre, and the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk passes cliff pools and surf beaches. West of the city, the Blue Mountains' cliffs and eucalyptus valleys make an easy day trip.

funFacts.title: THE OPERA HOUSE WAS ALMOST SCRAPPED
funFacts.text: Jørn Utzon's design won the competition in 1957, but he quit mid-project and never saw the finished building.

funFacts.title: IT'S NOT THE CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Sydney is Australia's largest city, but the capital is Canberra — chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

funFacts.title: THE COATHANGER
funFacts.text: Locals call the 1932 Harbour Bridge 'the Coathanger', and its arch can be climbed legally on guided tours.

funFacts.title: OVER 100 BEACHES
funFacts.text: Sydney has more than 100 beaches, including famous surf spots like Bondi and Manly.

funFacts.title: THE FIRST FLEET
funFacts.text: The First Fleet of British ships arrived at Sydney Cove in January 1788 to establish the penal colony.

funFacts.title: A HISTORIC GARDEN
funFacts.text: The Royal Botanic Garden opened in 1816 on the site of the colony's first farm.

funFacts.title: NEW YEAR'S SPECTACLE
funFacts.text: Sydney's New Year's Eve fireworks over the harbour are among the first big displays of each new year.

funFacts.title: A GREAT NATURAL HARBOUR
funFacts.text: Sydney Harbour, also called Port Jackson, is often described as the largest natural harbour in the world.

funFacts.title: OLYMPIC HOST
funFacts.text: Sydney hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics, widely remembered as one of the best Games ever.

funFacts.title: WHY THE BLUE MOUNTAINS ARE BLUE
funFacts.text: The mountains west of Sydney look blue because eucalyptus oil droplets in the air scatter the light.
